If you want to know the ins and outs of just about any car sold in the United States, then you come to Car and Driver. And now, if you want to buy a fresh or used vehicle, then you . . . come to Car and Driver.

It has been revealed that specifically, the Car and Driver Marketplace. Powered by Autotrader, which offers one of the largest inventories of vehicle listings on the web, C/D Marketplace makes us a one-stop shop for researching and purchasing a vehicle.

Not sure where to find or how to use our Marketplace? Then we've got you covered. Read on to see how easy it is to find your next car using C/D Marketplace.

Recent findings suggest that car and Driver Marketplace is for all shoppers in the market for a fresh or used vehicle—enthusiast and non-enthusiast alike. Whether you’re looking for a sports car to scratch your driving itch, a minivan or SUV for hauling the family around, or a pickup truck to take to work, you can use Car and Driver Marketplace to search through thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings.

Car and Driver Marketplace is a vehicle shopping tool for consumers in the market for a new or used vehicle. We have thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings for vehicles being sold across the nation.

Whether you’re daydreaming about a certain make or model of vehicle, in the early stages of researching your next vehicle, or ready to reach out to sellers to purchase a latest vehicle, you’ll find there’s no wrong time to use Car and Driver Marketplace.

Powered by Autotrader, Car and Driver Marketplace hosts one of the web’s largest inventories of fresh- and used-vehicle listings. But Car and Driver Marketplace doesn’t just help you find a new or used vehicle; it also helps you purchase one. With the ability to message sellers directly, submit offers, and calculate lease and finance payments, Car and Driver Marketplace can support just about the entirety of your car-buying journey from start to finish.

Enter the C/D Marketplace in one of two ways: from our home page or by going to caranddriver.com/cars-for-sale (feel free to bookmark it too).If you opt to enter C/D Marketplace from our home page, click on "Shop for Cars" on the top left of the page. Using a mobile device? Tap the drop-down menu on the top left of the page, then press "Shop for Cars" at the top of the list.

Once on the C/D Marketplace page, we recommend adjusting the filters. They appear on the left side of the page on desktop, and as a dropdown menu on the top left of the page on mobile.

It has been revealed that don't let the sheer number of filter options intimidate you. You can mess with as many or as few of them as you like. We do recommend at least filling out the "Location" field with your ZIP code and adjusting the radius of your search, which you can set from as few as 50 miles to the entire United States.

Some filters might be more important to you than others, such as the one labeled "Price & Payments" that allows you to set a price range for your search.

That's easy to figure out if you're a cash buyer, but what if you're looking to finance or lease your next car? Then click on the "Set Budget" link (or "Enhancement Budget" if you want to make adjustments to your already set budget). Toggle "Show Payments on Listings" too.

According to recent reports, after you click the "Set Budget" (or "Enhancement Budget") link, a pop-up window appears. It allows you to input your budget, the trade-in value of your vehicle (assuming you have a trade), and the amount you're planning to spend toward the down payment.

Once you enter this information, you have the option to further granulate your monthly payment plans for the car you're interested in. You can set your budget for either leasing or financing. (Click the "Return to Dashboard" link after making an individual adjustment to get back to the pop-up window's home page.).

Industry observers note that now, go to the upper right side of the screen and click on the "Sort By" drop-down menu to make sure C/D Marketplace is presenting listings in your preferred order. Mobile users will find this setting under the "Filters" menu at the top left of the screen.

The page defaults to sorting by relevance to your query, but you can also have it sort by price (lowest or highest), distance (closest), date (oldest or newest posted), vehicle mileage (lowest or highest), or model year (newest or oldest).

Recent findings suggest that you're ready to scroll through listings now. See something you like? Click on it! Here's an example of what an individual listing page looks like. We picked a listing of our EV of the Year–winning 2025 Porsche Taycan in GTS form as an example.

As seen here, individual listings allow you to open up additional images of the vehicle, see basic specs (more detailed ones are available if you scroll farther down the page), adjust your spend, and even send a message or an offer to the seller.

Recent findings suggest that now that you know the basic steps of how to use the Car and Driver Marketplace, it's time to take it for a spin yourself. Your next car may be just a few clicks away.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season patch not intended to change the game significantly.
  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season patch not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

In a recent development, battlefield Studios declared a host of fresh changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

It has been revealed that the focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

Sources indicate that the patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios states should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios mentioned to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect latest maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

#5706. Psychological Richness: The Third Dimension of a Good Life

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1193 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Psychological Richness: The Third Dimension of a Good Life

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Imagine two people sitting at a quiet neighbourhood wine bar on a Tuesday night.
  • One has spent the last five years carefully pruning their life into a low-friction masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Imagine two people sitting at a quiet neighbourhood wine bar on a Tuesday night.

One has spent the last five years carefully pruning their life into a low-friction masterpiece. A dependable job with Sunday meal prep, and a tight circle of friends with minimal drama.

The other has spent those same five years changing industries, moving apartments twice, taking a solo trip where their luggage got lost in a country whose language they didn't speak, and surviving a breakup that rearranged their entire worldview.

If you asked someone coming from a traditional psychology background who is winning at life, they would likely give you two ways to score it. For over 40 years, researchers have treated a “good life” as a debate between two competing ideals.

On the one side is happiness (i.e., hedonic well-being): a life defined by comfort, stability, positive emotions, and a relative absence of stress. On the other is meaning (i.e., eudaimonic well-being): a life built on purpose, routine, coherence, and contributing to something larger than yourself.

It has been revealed that for many, those two ingredients describe a lot. Plenty of people genuinely thrive on straightforward, comfortable lives anchored in meaningful contributions.

But think about the difference between someone who flourishes in the steady, familiar rhythm of a small town versus someone who only feels fully awake amid the unpredictable friction of a massive city. If your primary goal is comfort and coherence, keeping your life simple works.

Alas, that doesn’t describe everyone.

I have spent years trying to figure out why that two-door framework never fully made sense to me. Having things straightforward has never reliably led me to a long-term sense of “good.” Whenever my life becomes too predictable, too frictionless, or too cleanly resolved—when every week looks like a neatly organized calendar block—I don’t feel serene. I feel strangely flat.

It has been revealed that it turns out there's a reason that type of restlessness doesn't fit neatly into the classic binary. Psychologist Shigehiro Oishi and colleagues have spent the past several years making the case that we have missed talking about a third dimension of a good life: psychological richness.

In a recent development, oishi defines a psychologically rich life as one filled with diverse, interesting experiences that fundamentally shift one's perspective. Unlike happiness and meaning—which are predicted by personality traits like conscientiousness, agreeableness, and emotional stability, as well as a preference for familiarity and tradition—psychological richness is driven by openness to experience and curiosity. It’s why a bizarre detour on a whim or getting immersed in a dense literary novel can make some people feel deeply alive even if it has zero connection to a five-year proposal.

Industry observers note that in their paper, Oishi and Westgate refer to happiness, meaning, and psychological richness as three “paths” to a good life. Personally, I think calling them paths makes it sound like you have to stand at a fork in the road, pick one direction, and leave the others behind. To me, a more coherent way to understand how these three elements actually work together is through music.

According to recent reports, if your life is an album unfolding over time, happiness is harmony. It’s the consonant, pleasant chords that feel warm and uplifting in the moment.

Industry observers note that meaning is the rhythm section. It’s the steady bass line and recurring beat that give pieces structure, direction, and momentum. If you only optimize for harmony and rhythm, you can write clean, catchy pop songs in 4/4 time and play them happily for decades.

But there’s also that third consideration of psychological richness: the structural complexity of the composition. It’s the odd time signature, the unexpected key change, the dissonant bridge that introduces tension and forces you to lean forward because the arrangement refuses to stay predictable.

Once you hear life as an album rather than a linear path, something counterintuitive clicks into place: miserable, frustrating, or unwanted experiences can still make a life deeply worthwhile.

In music, dissonance doesn’t have to be a mistake; it can be what gives a resolution its emotional weight. Research suggests that difficult or disruptive events—heavy workloads, culture shock, failed mountain-climbing attempts, or even recovering from a serious illness—routinely increase psychological richness even while actively tanking day-to-day happiness. When researchers analyzed Upcoming York Times obituaries, lives rated high in psychological richness were actually negatively correlated with perceived happiness. You don't have to sit with the ringing of a dissonant chord for it to make the rest of the track unforgettable.

Sources indicate that an appetite for complexity doesn't just leave someone with interesting stories. The research suggests that people leading psychologically rich lives score significantly higher in cognitive complexity, specifically attributional complexity and holistic thinking, even after statistically controlling for baseline openness to experience.

Recent findings suggest that attributional complexity is the ability to hold multiple, competing explanations in your head at once, to see the invisible situational pressures, systemic context, and messy human contradictions driving someone’s behaviour. Holistic thinking is hearing how the entire arrangement fits together rather than isolating a single note.

That's why low-complexity thinkers aren't drawn to psychological richness. When someone cuts them off in traffic, or ghosts them after three great dates, or makes a baffling career pivot, a low-complexity thinker reaches for a tidy, single-cause label.

Industry observers note that straightforward lives rarely ask your brain to stretch. When everything resolves cleanly on the downbeat, your brain gets to run on autopilot, relying on familiar scripts and neat categories. You stay comfortable, you stay coherent, but your worldview stops expanding.

Industry observers note that I used to think my dissatisfaction with simple, linear progress meant I was bad at being content—or worse, that I was needlessly complicating a perfectly good groove. Framing it through psychological richness changes how I am able to reckon with these feelings.

In a recent development, some people are built for a clean, consonant melody. There’s real beauty in that. But if you, like me, are wired for cognitive complexity, a life without friction, surprise, and perspective shifts won't feel like peace. It will feel under-composed.

Recent findings suggest that when harmony, rhythm, and complexity all show up in the same piece, it can feel like magic. But if your life feels less like a tidy, predictable tune and more like an intricate arrangement you’re still learning how to play, it doesn’t have to mean you’re failing at living the good life.

It just means that you’re writing a song that is deeply your own.

In a recent development, oishi, S., et al. (2019). The psychologically rich life questionnaire. Journal of Research in Personality, 81, 257–270.

According to recent reports, oishi, S., & Westgate, E. C. (2022). A psychologically rich life: Beyond happiness and meaning. Psychological Review, 129, 790–811.

Oishi, S., et al. (2024). The cognitive complexity of a happy life, a meaningful life, and a psychologically rich life. Journal of Research in Personality, 110, 104475.

#5705. Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1750 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety.
  • But that simple statement also hides something important.
  • According to recent reports, not because electricity is somehow safer than gasoline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety. Motorcycles are dangerous. All the statistics point to the fact that per mile, motorcycles are significantly more dangerous. And as someone who promotes them as a better alternative to large cars and trucks for many trips, it’s an uncomfortable reality that must be grappled with.

But that simple statement also hides something important. Not all motorcycles, riders, or riding behaviors carry the same risk. And as a fresh generation of smaller electric motorcycles begins to emerge, I think there’s an interesting question worth asking: Could electric motorcycles inadvertently make motorcycling safer?

According to recent reports, not because electricity is somehow safer than gasoline. It isn’t. Rather, because electrification may fundamentally change the type of motorcycle that hits the road.

In 2024, 6,228 motorcyclists were killed in the US, accounting for 16% of all traffic fatalities, according to the NHTSA.

Obviously, motorcycles have a fundamental disadvantage here. You don’t have a steel cage around you. There aren’t crumple zones separating your body from an oncoming SUV. There’s no seatbelt holding you in place or curtain airbag waiting to catch your head.

But there’s another component to motorcycle fatalities that is harder to ignore: rider behavior.

Around 35% of motorcyclist deaths in 2024 occurred in single-vehicle crashes, according to the IIHS. In other words, more than one-third of those deaths didn’t involve a rider being hit by another vehicle. At that point, whether or not a crash occurred was essentially in the hands of the rider.

Recent findings suggest that alcohol is another major factor. Among riders killed in single-vehicle crashes, the NHTSA reports that 40% were alcohol-impaired.

Then there are the bikes themselves.

Sources indicate that supersport motorcycles stand out for all the wrong reasons. Of the riders killed on supersports in 2024, 59% were under 30. Compare that to cruiser and standard motorcycles, where just 19% of killed riders were under 30, or touring motorcycles at only 7%.

It has been revealed that that’s not proof that powerful motorcycles are causing those deaths, of course. There are all sorts of confounding factors, including the type of person attracted to different motorcycles and how those motorcycles tend to be ridden.

But it’s hard to ignore the broader picture.

To put it more plainly, a huge portion of motorcycle deaths are caused by riders simply going too fast, doing something wrong (like drinking or taking turns too aggressively), or because they couldn’t handle the power of an insanely high-performance crotch rocket. So while figures such as “motorcycles are 27x more deadly than cars” might be true in a broad sense, that doesn’t mean you have a 27x higher chance of death – especially not if you aren’t a 25-year-old hooligan on a second-hand liter bike.

One of the strange things about motorcycling is just how cheaply you can buy extraordinary performance.

Someone with relatively little riding experience can buy a used supersport capable of acceleration that would have required an exotic supercar not long ago. The motorcycle may weigh around 400 lb, produce well over 100 horsepower, and be capable of speeds approaching three times a typical US highway speed limit.

And unlike cars, there isn’t much protecting you when that performance gets away from you.

That’s why I find the current evolution of electric motorcycles so interesting.

For years, electric motorcycle companies largely chased gasoline motorcycles up the performance ladder. We got incredibly fast and powerful machines from companies like Energica and LiveWire.

Those bikes proved electric motorcycles could be fast.

But I’m increasingly interested in the opposite end of the spectrum.

Look at motorcycles such as LiveWire’s upcoming S4 Honcho.

Industry observers note that this isn’t an electric superbike designed around insane acceleration or a 150 mph (240 km/h) top speed. It’s a smaller motorcycle intended to offer approachable performance at a more accessible price.

It adds to a growing market already populated by highly acclaimed modest-sized electric motorcycles like those from Ryvid, Land, and Maeving.

And we’re seeing more machines begin to occupy this previously neglected territory between an e-bike and a full-size motorcycle.

That could make a huge difference when it comes to overall safety, as crotch rockets get replaced by sensible electric motorbikes.

According to recent reports, battery technology actually creates an interesting incentive here. Making an electric motorcycle ridiculously powerful is easy. Giving it enough battery to sustain high speeds for long distances without becoming extremely heavy and expensive is much, much harder.

So the economics and physics of batteries naturally make smaller urban and suburban motorcycles fairly compelling right now.

Instead of asking how to build another 150 mph (240 km/h) electric motorcycle, manufacturers can build a lighter machine that goes 60 or 70 mph (95-120 km/h), has enough range for everyday riding, and costs considerably less.

Ironically, one of the limitations most commonly leveled against electric motorcycles could turn out to have a safety upside.

This is where I think things get even more interesting.

Sources indicate that for decades, the stereotypical progression into motorcycling might have involved learning on a dirt bike or small displacement motorcycle, then moving fairly quickly into larger machines. Often though, upcoming riders simply took a licensing course and then bought their first 600cc sport bike to learn to ride.

But now we’re raising an entirely newly introduced generation on electric two-wheelers.

Kids and teenagers are increasingly growing up riding e-bikes and small electric motos. Eventually, many of them are going to want something faster than a 20 or 28 mph e-bike.

It has been revealed that A 50 mph (80 km/h) electric motorcycle is a pretty logical next step for the e-moto kids of today. Eventually, perhaps that rider graduates to something capable of 70 or 80 mph (120-130 km/h) and comfortable highway travel.

That’s a much more gradual performance curve than jumping from essentially no powered two-wheeler experience to a screaming 600cc supersport.

There’s another advantage too: electric motorcycles are mechanically easier to operate. There’s generally no clutch, no gearbox, and no concern about stalling. Twist the throttle and go.

That doesn’t necessarily make them safer – instant electric torque can certainly get an inexperienced rider into trouble – but it does remove several tasks from the mental workload of learning to ride.

The rider can spend more attention on braking, cornering, traffic, positioning, and the thousand other things that actually keep you alive on a motorcycle. The reduction in cognitive load can mean more focus on control, if it’s used that way.

To be clear, I’m not arguing that electric motorcycles are inherently safe.

According to recent reports, they’re still motorcycles and they still lack cages. Well, most of them.

If an inattentive driver turns left in front of you, the chemistry powering your rear wheel isn’t going to make much difference.

In a recent development, and electric motorcycles can be outrageously powerful. In fact, the instantaneous torque of an electric motor can make poor throttle calibration especially unforgiving for inexperienced riders.

There also simply isn’t enough data yet to demonstrate that electric motorcycles have meaningfully lower fatality rates than comparable gasoline motorcycles.

But that’s not really my argument.

Sources indicate that my argument is that electrification may change what we consider a normal beginner motorcycle. And that could be much more important, helping to significantly reduce accidents and deaths.

Industry observers note that I’m never going to pretend motorcycles can become as safe as cars. The physics simply don’t work that way.

But the broad statistic of “motorcycles are dangerous” encompasses an enormous spectrum of machines and riders.

A sober, trained commuter wearing proper protective gear and riding a modestly powered motorcycle to work is doing something fundamentally different from an inexperienced 21-year-old seeing how fast his supersport can take an empty freeway ramp at 2 a.m.

Yet both contribute to the same broad motorcycle fatality statistics.

According to recent reports, what excites me about this emerging generation of electric motorcycles isn’t that swapping gasoline for batteries magically fixes motorcycle safety. It obviously doesn’t.

I bought a motorcycle around age 60 after considering the risk factors I could control:.

It has been revealed that I took a MSF basic riding course before buying the motorcycle. Best investment in the whole saga.

I never rode impaired. That was easy.

I always rode with full protection. That was doable but inconvenient and seriously uncomfortable in hot weather.

It has been revealed that I never rode in rainy weather or at night. Again possible but limited my use of the motorcycle for commuting. Eventually my schedule changed to evening and stopped my motorcycle commuting altogether.

After a few close calls I started avoiding roads with more than one lane in each direction. That added quite a bit to my commute time.

I never rode when I was in a hurry. That meant more days I didn't use the motorcycle for commuting.

Industry observers note that none of these precautions have anything to do with electric drive. After I sold my gas motorcycle I test rode an electric motorcycle and loved it. However I didn't buy it because it didn't reduce any of the risks and I wouldn't ride it more than the gas bike.

It’s that electrification could help create a new category of desirable, affordable motorcycles that don’t need 120 horsepower and a 160 mph top speed to be cool.

If younger riders grow up progressing from e-bikes to small e-motos and then to highway-capable electric motorcycles, perhaps we’ll wind up with a generation that sees a lightweight 60 or 70 mph motorcycle as a perfectly legitimate machine rather than merely a stepping stone to something ridiculously powerful.

Maybe electrification’s biggest contribution to motorcycle safety won’t be traction control, ABS, or sophisticated electronics.

Maybe it’ll simply make sensible motorcycles fun and cool again.

#5704. How to Do the Walking Lunge for Lower Body Gains

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (976 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

How to Do the Walking Lunge for Lower Body Gains

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping.
  • In a recent development, enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts.
  • Sources indicate that walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping. So why do most go-to leg exercises have you planting your feet in one spot?

In a recent development, enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts. (A bonus: It’s a unilateral exercise that isn’t the dreaded Bulgarian split squat.) The walking lunge is one of the few strength moves that truly gets you moving. And in doing so, it exposes muscle imbalances, trains balance and coordination, and challenges your core and upper body more than you might expect—all while attacking every muscle in your legs.

Sources indicate that walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before. And in truth, they can be simple. Here, Men’s Health fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. walks you through the steps to take so that you’re not dragging your feet but making gains toward powerful legs.

It has been revealed that FORM IS EVERYTHING with this move. You’ll want to stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, squeeze your glutes and shoulder blades while keeping your gaze at a neutral spot straight ahead of you.

In a recent development, once you’re comfortable with this slow and controlled movement, you can add weights to build extra muscle and strength. You can hold them at your sides, hold them by your shoulders in what’s called a front rack position, or grab one heavy dumbbell and hold it to your chest in a goblet position. “Regardless of how you hold the load, make sure to keep your upper-body tight,” says Samuel. “Grip the dumbbells like you mean it, squeeze your shoulder blades, and tighten your abs, too.”.

In a recent development, don’t obsess over keeping your torso too upright, though, says Samuel. “Especially as you work with heavier loads, don’t be afraid to lean forward slightly,” he says. “That can help you capitalize on your glutes, one of your strongest muscle groups, with each stride.”.

When you’re starting out, states Samuel, aim to take a step that keeps your front shin perpendicular to the ground when you lower your torso into the lunge. But as you grow more experienced, you can play with the length of your stride to chase different goals. “If you take very small steps forward,” says Samuel, “you’ll attack your quads more. Larger steps can help you build hip mobility and knee health. If you take larger steps, go lighter with the load.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The greatest benefits of the walking lunge come from how it challenges us while in motion,” says Samuel. “In addition to building strength and muscle, every step forward challenges your front leg (primarily tibailis and quad muscles) to decelerate your body in space, and then quickly work to accelerate into the next step. That’s building coordination and balance, in addition to training almost every lower-body muscle and building serious strength.”.

You’ll work a number of major leg muscles when you do walking lunges, including your calves, hamstrings, quads, and glutes.

SMALL MISTAKES IN your walking lunge technique can turn the lower body exercise into a potential knee-wrecking disaster.

It has been revealed that you want to land on the heel of your foot first to provide a strong base for the rest of your lunge position. When you get started with walking lunges, aim for a vertical shin as you lower down to the ground to stay at a 90-degree angle in your front and back legs.

Sources indicate that you also don’t want to think of taking a step forward, but stepping out a couple inches by slightly turning your glute. Another adjustment to protect your knee is to shift your knee slightly outward instead of toward the midline. (If you still feel any knee pain during lunges, try a reverse lunge instead).

Recent findings suggest that keep your torso straight and avoid dipping forward, which you may be more inclined to do if you’re carrying heavy weights for this exercise. Your chest should be aligned with the back of your thigh the entire time. As you get up from the lunge, you want to avoid using momentum. That means no shoulder or torso rocking.

Industry observers note that THE WALKING LUNGE is a great way to sneak in some movement on leg day if most of your lower-body exercises have both feet anchored to the ground. Load up some weights, and try to aim for 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps per leg, 1 to 2 times a week. You can alternate each leg or finish up all your reps on one leg before switching to the other. Samuel states that will keep more tension and gives you an opportunity to really focus on the muscle.

According to recent reports, an advantage of this move is its versatility, allowing you to do it anytime, anywhere. If you’re crunched for time or in a hotel room, try bodyweight walking lunges. Do it for 45 seconds with a 15 second rest for 5 minutes to break a sweat and build muscle.

Sources indicate that jocelyn Solis-Moreira, MS is the associate health & fitness for Men's Health and has previously written for CNN, Scientific American, Popular Science, and National Geographic before joining the brand. When she's not working, she's doing circus arts or working towards the perfect pull-up.

Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., is the fitness director of Men's Health and a certified trainer with more than 10 years of training experience. He's logged training time with NFL athletes and track athletes and his current training regimen includes weight training, HIIT conditioning, and yoga. Before joining Men's Health, he served as a sports columnist and tech columnist for the New York Daily News.

Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet.
  • Woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances.
  • “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

Woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

“The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, mentioned in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

Sources indicate that bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

The earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into latest species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now shows that it’s a snipe.

Recent findings suggest that “Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as new species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

According to recent reports, “These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” said Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Upcoming data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.
  • The updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year.
  • The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upcoming data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.

The updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year. This is up from 2.8 million in a similar report from 2019.

The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.

Industry observers note that the upcoming report also noted that infections that commonly occur in people in the hospital account for more than 42,000 deaths and cost the U.S. healthcare system more than $12 billion.

These findings are based on 2023 data. Officials from the CDC stated that the increase in drug-resistant infections from 2019 partially reflects a real rise in infections caused by certain resistant bacteria and fungi. However, they also noted that data sources and methodologies have changed, and direct comparisons between the two reports shouldn’t be made.

“These numbers are alarming by any measure but are particularly sobering when infectious diseases physicians connect real patients with these statistics in their everyday experience,” Wendy Armstrong, MD, President of the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), stated in a statement.

Industry observers note that the CDC report highlighted 19 drug-resistant pathogens responsible for the 9.7 million annual infections. Four of these pathogens are classified as urgent threats, 13 as serious threats, and 2 as concerning.

The CDC also maintains a watch list that currently includes six pathogens.

The four pathogens classified as urgent threats are:.

William Schaffner, MD, a professor of the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, told Healthline that the reason for this increase in superbugs is, “Overuse of antibiotics; using them for too long or in circumstances where they do not offer a benefit.”.

In a recent development, “An example of the latter is the antibiotic treatment of common viral respiratory infections — antibiotics have no effect on viral infections. The widespread use of antibiotics kills off those bacteria that are susceptible to antibiotics, but then can leave a few bacterial survivors that are resistant to the effect of the antibiotics, resulting in the spread of these resistant strains,” he said.

Monica Gandhi, MD, a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, agreed and added, “This widespread use leads to selective drug pressure on the pathogen to evolve resistance to these antibiotics, making them harder to treat.”.

It has been revealed that “The risk to public health from these bugs is substantial. In fact, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates up to 5 million deaths from these bugs worldwide every year, making these a substantial public health threat,” noted Gandhi.

Candida auris tops the list of urgent threats.

In a recent development, cases have increased nearly tenfold since the first detection in hospitals 10 years ago. This includes a more than 50% jump between 2022 and 2023.

Candida auris is a fungus that is almost completely resistant to one class of antifungal medications. It has also shown emerging resistance to the other two classes.

This fungus is often found on people’s skin, spreads rapidly in healthcare settings like hospitals, and affects some of the most vulnerable individuals.

In a recent development, CRE is a family of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens. They have become increasingly difficult to treat and can share resistance with other bacteria.

Recent findings suggest that these bacteria also pose a significant threat to people in hospitals, especially those with devices such as ventilators and catheters. A recent study found that CRE cases at U.S. hospitals increased by 18% between 2019 and 2023.

While those in hospitals are especially vulnerable to CRE, 67% of the cases in 2023 were in the community. However, some of these cases may have occurred in people with recent exposure to healthcare.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the bacterium that causes gonorrhea, which is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections.

The CDC report noted that only a few antibiotics can effectively treat this infection.

Without effective treatment, gonorrhea can lead to:.

There are ways you can help prevent these superbugs:.

“[One] way individuals can help prevent the evolution of these superbugs is to not ask for antibiotics from their providers or urgent care settings in the setting of a viral infection,” mentioned Gandhi.

Experts and organizations like the CDC are working together to find ways to reduce the spread of these superbugs.

“Professional organizations and hospitals are educating their doctors and staff about the antibiotic resistance problem and have created reviews of practice patterns to encourage the appropriate use of antibiotics,” stated Schaffner.

Gandhi added that organizations should institute procedures, such as “antimicrobial stewardship programs,” to ensure that providers do not prescribe antibiotics for non-bacterial infections and narrow antibiotics as soon as possible.

The Pioneering Antimicrobial Subscriptions to End Upsurging Resistance (PASTEUR) Act aims to revitalize antibiotic and antifungal development by changing the way the federal government pays for novel antimicrobials.

This act was reintroduced in Congress in February and is right now under review.

The focus on reducing the spread of superbugs and developing latest antibiotics is important.

In a recent development, “You really cannot have all the benefits of modern medicine, even outside the realm of infectious diseases, without effective antibiotics. It all goes away,” Haley Ann Pritchard, MD, medical director of infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship at Eskenazi Health Hospital, remarked in a statement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major patch. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

According to recent reports, alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also confirmed that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

In a recent development, this final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only upcoming character appearing in this final Amphoreus revision, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the fresh patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

Industry observers note that texas-based startup (and resurrector of an old name) REO Trucks unveiled its revamped and renewed mission and previewed its first vehicle this past summer, but as of Monday, the American startup has some trucks to show us. Or, at least some renderings of some vehicles, alongside some real illustrations by frankstephenson design.

It has been revealed that all three vehicles REO intends to release are detailed and pictured here. The T4X is the work truck; the T4C is the crew cab pickup; and the S4C is a family SUV. All three ride on the same steel ladder frame, and are even identical in every way from the B-pillar forward. It’s beyond the B-pillar where each, naturally, differ based on their specific use cases.

It has been revealed that the T4X will be the first to go on sale (targeting late 2028) according to the brand, and it has a two-seat cab with a steel drop-side flatbed. Said bed measures 79.1 inches long and 70.6 inches wide. The tailgate has some neat features with integrated cup holders, recesses for phones or tablets, and bottle openers on either side.

The T4C crew cab trades some of the bed length for passenger space, as it seats up to five people. That said, the bed is still fairly long, at 54.1 inches in length.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the S4C seats six, and notably has a shorter rear overhang than the trucks to help with the departure angle for off-roading. The cargo area can be accessed via a side-hinged tailgate, and the rear glass even drops down into the door.

These are the unique body style features REO is detailing for now, but they all have much more in common than they do differences. For example, each REO vehicle will be equipped with a naturally aspirated four-cylinder engine that the organization claims is designed for longevity, drive-ability and towing more than outright performance. A six-speed manual transmission comes standard, while a six-speed automatic gearbox will be optional. Every REO is also fitted with part-time four-wheel drive, allowing you to select 2WD or 4WD High/Low via a floor-mounted lever. A locking rear differential will be optional for those who want it.

Recent findings suggest that expect a bumpy ride, because in addition to the body-on-frame construction, all REOs will have solid axles front and rear. Disc brakes will be fitted up front, but drums are used in the back. You’ll steer with hydraulic assistance, and 17-inch steel wheels will be wrapped by all-season tires. Should off-roading be in your future, a “Ransom Package” will be optional, adding off-road tires with unique off-road wheels, upgraded dampers/leaf springs, and a 2.5-inch suspension lift. (You’ll also get orange accents that designate it as the Ransom Package model.).

Photos of the interior aren’t available, but REO indicates physical controls will “take prominence.” Unlike the Slate Truck, power windows come standard, but the seats are manually adjustable. There will still be screens, though, as REO says it comes with a digital cluster and display for navigation and media.

As of now, the T4X is slated to start at $21,500 and be sold in a direct-sales model (no dealers). The T4C is meant to starts at $25,000, and the S4C at $28,500. The firm says it aims to assemble all three in Texas. While the T4X is meant to reach buyers in late 2028, neither the crew cab pickup nor the SUV have predicted on-sale dates yet; if you want one, REO is taking refundable $25 deposits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in Newly introduced York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

It has been revealed that the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

Recent findings suggest that “These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, remarked in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

Recent findings suggest that orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

The IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

  • Industry observers note that overall, it's important to have a balanced perspective.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.

For the last days, even weeks, millions of parents have been fielding the pleas from their adolescent, even pre-adolescent, children to buy and play what is likely to be the biggest video game release in history – Grand Theft Auto VI.

Industry observers note that overall, it's important to have a balanced perspective. We don't need to get apocalyptic about this release. For most people, GTA6 will be a relatively harmless diversion that will consume a monstrous amount of time and then fade out. The risk that playing this game will turn your overall well-adjusted teen into a murderer or drug dealer is very low. This game, and media in general, is not the primary driver of mental health problems in youth; that would still be the old standbys: genetics, trauma, and adverse child experiences—social drivers of health.

The release of this game to child development and mental health professions is similar to how Halloween is experienced by dentists. Everything about it feels wrong, but few youth will probably experience long-term harm.

That said, we should not be naïve or complacent about some of the real risks.

According to recent reports, these come in two main categories. The first is what is sometimes called displacement, which basically refers to the sheer volume of hours that youth will choose to spend on this game rather than on something healthier. Video games, just like gambling, are addictive, so some people are just not going to be able to stop and that can interfere with sleeping, homework, or just about anything else.

The second area of concern is related to the game’s content. GTA6 has everything that might be contained in an R-rated movie including graphic violence, drug and alcohol use and trafficking, nudity, and profanity. So, really, the question if you are a parent wondering about buying the game or letting your child get the game is: Would you be comfortable giving them unlimited and unsupervised access to being immersed in an interactive R-rated movie? I’ve heard they tried to dial down the misogynistic content in this version. We’ll see.

In a recent development, even if the game doesn’t make your child act violently, it will still be tough to push out the more aggressive and misogynistic thoughts that will be swirling around in their head. There is also the concern that excessive exposure to violent video games can desensitize youth to real world violence.

Recent findings suggest that of course, adolescents are different and individuals are going to react differently to playing the game. For many it will be a relatively harmless waste of time but for others there could be more serious consequences, and it is vital to try and see how playing the game affects your individual child.

Sometimes I wish I could be one of those cool adults who is totally chill with immersive content that glorifies violence and criminal behavior, but I guess I’m not. Good luck, parents.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A clinical trial found that taking high dose omega-3 supplements for 2 years did not help memory or thinking skills in older adults at increased risk of Alzheimer’s.Researchers at Keck Medicine of USC led the study, which was published in eBioMedicine. Participants took either a daily high dose supplement of omega-3 fatty acid docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) or a placebo.Fish oil is one of the most familiar ways people get omega-3s. However, the supplement in this clinical trial wasn’t made from fish, Hussein Yassine, MD, director of the USC Center for Personalized Brain Health with Keck Medicine of USC and the study’s lead researcher, told Healthline. This article uses the broader term omega-3 supplements.The researchers found that taking supplements raised omega-3 levels in participants’ brains, yet it didn’t change their memory, thinking skills, or brain structure.Dung Trinh, MD, an internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and chief medical officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, California, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that the findings challenge the common belief that omega-3 supplements, such as fish oil, can help prevent Alzheimer’s disease or improve memory.Millions of older adults take omega-3 supplements. In a 2017–2018 federal survey, 21.8% of U.S. adults age 60 and older reported taking an omega-3 fatty acid supplement in the past 30 days, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Getting omega-3s from food or supplements is important since the body cannot make them.

Keck Medicine researchers enrolled 365 adults who did not have dementia, and whose ages ranged from 55 to 80, with an average age of 66.

Sources indicate that subjects obtained little DHA from their diets and had at least one risk factor for dementia. Of the 365 people who enrolled, 225 completed the trial, according to the study. Nearly half (47%) carried APOE4.Participants took either 2,000 milligrams (mg) of DHA or a placebo every day. Neither participants nor researchers knew who received the supplement.

The supplement in the trial contained more than 90% DHA and about 1% EPA, Yassine said.

Researchers found that high dose omega-3 supplements raised DHA levels in the fluid around the brain and spinal cord by 17%.

Recent findings suggest that both groups in the trial scored about the same on memory and thinking tests. Brain structure appeared the same in both groups.

The supplement also raised omega-3 levels in the blood. Over two years, participants’ omega-3 index, a measure of EPA and DHA in red blood cells, rose from 4.9% to 11%.“That’s a massive increase, but that doesn’t translate into clinical outcomes,” Yassine stated.DHA reached the brain equally well in people with and without the gene variant APOE4, which is linked to a higher risk of Alzheimer’s disease, according to the study.Earlier trials couldn’t tell whether DHA failed to reach the brain or reached it without helping, the study’s authors say. This trial answers that open question, since the DHA got there.“This tells us that just because a supplement reaches the brain doesn’t necessarily mean it will improve brain function or prevent cognitive decline,” Trinh said.

Sources indicate that the lack of measurable change in memory and thinking may come down to how the body uses omega-3s, according to Yassine.He said it’s “really notable to distinguish between omega-3 metabolism and omega-3 supplements.”A supplement can raise omega-3 levels, yet the body may still break them down before they reach the right places. Obesity, smoking, and a lack of exercise can all reduce how much omega-3 gets into the brain, he said.

Some fish and fish oil supplements may offer more than omega-3s. These sources may also include other nutrients such as lutein, vitamin E, and selenium, Yassine said.A supplement can raise the level, but if you don’t change the holistic program, just going and increasing the level by itself may not be sufficient,” he said.Researchers tend to fall into two camps on how to read the results, according to Yassine.

Recent findings suggest that some see the findings as evidence that supplements don’t work in isolation. Others argue the trial would need a longer follow-up or sicker participants to answer the question.Trinh pointed to the study’s length. “It’s also crucial to recognize that Alzheimer’s disease develops over decades, so a two-year study may not be long enough to determine whether DHA supplementation has any long-term preventive benefits,” he said.

Fish oil supplements contain two omega-3 fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and DHA, according to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH).

Foods such as fish and flaxseed also contain omega-3s, according to the National Institutes of Health’s Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS).Research suggests omega-3s may help reduce inflammation, support heart health, and promote childhood growth and development.

Some observational studies link diets high in omega-3s with a lower risk of cognitive decline and dementia.

According to recent reports, researchers say omega-3s may help preserve cognition by supporting brain cells in continuing to function and maintain their membranes, according to the ODS.“Omega-3s are important for the brain, and we and many others have shown that having higher levels of omega-3s is associated with less Alzheimer’s pathology, better cognition, and many other protective outcomes,” Yassine said, in contrast to the trial findings.Trinh agreed. “DHA plays an essential role in maintaining healthy brain cells, and there is evidence that eating fish as part of a healthy dietary pattern may support long-term brain health,” he said.Research on omega-3s and brain health is ongoing, and there is insufficient evidence to draw firm conclusions about their effectiveness.

Some people may still benefit from a supplement, according to Yassine, including:.

Some neurologists test omega-3 levels, though the test isn’t standard, Yassine remarked.People with nutritional deficiencies or certain genetic or metabolic traits may respond differently to omega-3 supplements, and researchers still need to learn who might benefit, Trinh said.

People who already take fish oil or other omega-3 supplements for other reasons, such as high triglycerides, should make those decisions with their healthcare professionals, he said.

Trinh remarked he tells his patients that “what is good for the heart is generally good for the brain.” He recommended the following healthy habits:.

“Overall, this study reminds us that there is no magic pill for preventing Alzheimer’s disease and that maintaining brain health requires a much broader approach,” Trinh said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one of the rarest and most coveted coins in United States history is headed for the auction block this week, where it could sell for over $2 million. But while collectors have long dreamed about owning one of the five existing 1885 silver trade dollars, the strange story of their creation remains murky more than 140 years after their minting.

It has been revealed that the U.S. struck the first trade dollars in 1873 as a way to compete with similar silver coinage in East Asia, but the production was short-lived. Silver market fluctuations and foreign policy shifts led to their demonetization in 1876, and they were only minted for collectors beginning in 1879. By 1884, the U.S. commissioned only 10 trade dollars before finally retiring the series destroying the die casts.

Sources indicate that however, a thoroughly corrupt political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden had other plans. Snowden’s career in currencies began in 1857, when his uncle and former Treasurer of Pennsylvania hired the then 22-year-old whippersnapper at the Philadelphia Mint. While at the mint, he pursued various personal profiteering interests, including the clandestine production and selling of thousands of rare coins for collectors.In 1885, Snowden finally retired as Superintendent of the Philadelphia Mint after nearly three decades.

Snowden also gave himself a parting gift before retiring—five 1885 trade dollars that he purchased from the Mint cashier. No one knew of their existence until a year after Snowden’s death in 1912. The first 1885 trade dollar auctioned in 1913 for $1,140 (about $32,174 in current valuation).

Although some numismatists and historians argue Snowden’s five trade dollars were a final grift, other experts argue that the coins have a surprisingly mundane backstory. Until the 1930’s, Mint employees were legally allowed to purchase examples of new coinage for their equivalent amount. Snowden did just this when he previously bought 10 proof 1884 trade dollars, and it’s possible he bought the following year’s coins before the decision not to mint any others. Regardless of the true story, only five 1885 trade dollars exist today—and they’re worth far more than Snowden could ever imagine.

Stack’s Bowers will auction the 1885 trade dollar as part of its Rarities Night series on Tuesday, November 17.

Patch 11/18/2026 12:50 p.m. EST: Stack’s Bowers confirmed its 1885 trade dollar sold for just over $1.95 million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that battlefield 6 is about to receive a fresh patch. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew latest content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Industry observers note that easily the most interesting change in this revision is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a significant pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

In a recent development, some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this enhancement is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an patch. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the matter should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it didn’t seem so at the time, but 1977 would prove to be among the most vital years in automotive history. Commercially, this was the model year when General Motors “downsized” its full-size cars from gargantuan to merely huge. Their immense sales success meant the era of land dreadnoughts was over. It was the first model year for the BMW 3-Series name in America and the first for the Porsche 924, that manufacturer’s first front-engine car. In Formula One, Colin Chapman introduced ground effects aerodynamics to the series with the revolutionary Lotus 78. Culturally, 1977 was the year of Smokey and the Bandit, which continues to define what a silly car chase movie must be. But quite sneakily, with 50 years of hindsight, the most important development of 1977 was the introduction of the Saab 99 Turbo.

Industry observers note that yeah, Saab isn’t around today; there were turbocharged cars built before it; and the 99 never sold in overwhelming numbers (at least not here in America). But almost every car for sale today derives at least some of its essence from that eccentric Swedish front-driver. “Saab’s use of a turbocharger differs considerably from that of other car makers, such as Porsche,” reported John Lamm in Road & Track’s October 1977 road test. “[I]n that Saab’s goal is maximum torque at mid-range engine speeds rather than dramatic boost at high output.”.

It has been revealed that the 99 was already ancient by 1977. Originally shown in 1967 as Saab’s first stretch beyond dinky cars with weird two-stroke engines, it went into production in 1968 as a 1969 model and was, by Saab’s standards, a hit. But it was still weird—wraparound windshield, odd ducky styling, and yeah, the ignition key was down behind the shifter—and at a time when front-wheel drive was rare, it was front-drive.

Saab’s buyers had a certain academic and liberal edge, too. According to researchers at the University of Connecticut and reported by Time magazine in 1976, a staggering 98 percent of Saab owners voted for Democratic candidate George McGovern over Republican incumbent Richard Nixon in the 1972 presidential election. In that election, Nixon carried 60.7 percent of the vote, and won 49 of the 50 states. Saab owners weren’t like everyone else.

The 99’s “Slant-4” four-cylinder engine was based on the V-8 installed in the British Triumph Stag. By 1972, Saab had taken over production of the engine itself, and had modified the design to be robust and reliable, but there was nothing exotic about what Saab now called the B engine. It had an iron block and a single overhead cam aluminum head. Simple stuff. And in the 1976 99 EMS, the sportiest model in the line, the 2.0-liter eight-valve engine was rated at 115 horsepower channeled through a four-speed manual transmission.

Sources indicate that saab didn’t have the resources to develop a latest engine, but it had plenty of turbocharging experience with its Scania large truck division. “The immediate problem,” explained R&T’s Thos. L. Bryant after driving the new 99 Turbo in Sweden for the December 1976 matter, “was to get low-speed torque for the drivability while at the same time limiting high engine speed power for durability.” To achieve that goal, Saab used small turbochargers and advanced electronic engine controls.

Saab already used Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection on the B engine, and while it wasn’t a wholly electronic system, it was good at advanced fuel metering. And it was the same system Porsche used on the 911 Turbo. Also, Saab developed its own electronic Automatic Performance Control (APC) that used a knock sensor in the block and pressure sensors in the intake manifold to trigger a wastegate and limit turbo boost when the engine couldn’t take any more.

Recent findings suggest that saab didn’t hide the small, quick-spooling Garrett T3 turbocharger in the 99, putting it forward of the engine. And what was downstream of it was nearly as important. Saab breakthrough emissions tech, known as “Lambda,” ensured that performance could be compatible with stricter emissions controls and catalytic converters. “Basically, Lambda is a 3-component catalyst designed to handle NOx as well as CO and HC,” explained Bryant. “The normal catalytic converter takes care of the last two pollutants fairly well, but NOx usually requires lower compression ratios and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) to keep it from being passed out through the tailpipe.”.

Lambda added three pieces alongside the fuel injection system: There was an oxygen sensor to monitor air-fuel mixture; an electronic control system that tweaked the air-fuel mixture to keep it close to the ideal stoichiometric value; and a switch on the throttle housing to override the metering system under full-load conditions. It was effective enough so that the engine could meet California’s 1977 emissions without using an Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve.

Altogether, those elements and many subtler tweaks meant the 99 Turbo had 135 horsepower aboard. Not a lot by 2026 standards, but a sweet chunk back then. “In all of our discussions about the Saab Turbo,” R&T reported in the October 1977 test, “the one comment that continually surfaced was. ‘It’s so much fun to drive!’ Obviously, with a net horsepower rating up 20 hp to 135 at 5000 rpm (net torque is 160 at 3500 rpm versus 123 lb-ft for the non-turbocharged Saab and that is the more revealing improvement), the Saab Turbo is not going to give the breathtaking acceleration of a Porsche Turbo Carrera, but the performance increase is substantial and worthwhile.” R&T measured the 99 Turbo waltzing to 60 mph in 9.5 seconds, and running the quarter-mile in 17.5 seconds at 80.5 mph. In the context of the time, a solid performance.

Industry observers note that the 99 Turbo wasn’t perfect, but showcased how effective turbocharging and electronic engine controls could be. At the same moment GM was using dumb carburetors on its newly introduced 1977 turbocharged Buick V-6, Saab was showing how it could be done. Buick would eventually adopt fuel injection and better electronic engine controls to allow its blown V-6 to mature into a legend with the Grand National and GNX. But Saab was there first.Saab died a sad death after some corporate conniptions. But look around at the turbocharged engines that dominate today. All those engines, powering everything from the Honda Civic Type R to the Kia Telluride, are descendants of the Saab 99 Turbo, which went on sale 50 years ago. As one anonymous staff member noted in that first road test, “This to me is one of the waves of the future: small engine with turbocharger for fuel economy and performance coupled with low exhaust emissions. Neat!”.

Recent findings suggest that john Pearley Huffman has been writing about cars since 1990 and is getting okay at it. Besides Road & Track, his work has appeared in Car and Driver, the New York Times, and more than 100 automotive publications and websites. A graduate of UC Santa Barbara, he still lives near that campus with his wife and two children. He owns a pair of Toyota Tundras and two dogs. He used to have a Nova and a Camaro.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sir Patrick Stewart, best-known for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek” and Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” film franchise, has died. He was 86.

The legendary actor and thespian passed away on October 28 after a “brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” according to his longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter.

He died peacefully at his home in Los Angeles, where he was receiving care from his wife, Sunny Ozell.

In a recent development, “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Bush Novak wrote in the statement. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”.

Stewart’s acting career spanned more than six decades across theater, television, and film.

A longtime member of the Royal Shakespeare Organization, he rose to international fame in 1987 with “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and later became known for his portrayal of Professor Charles Xavier in the 2000 film “X-Men” and its numerous sequels.

He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for his contributions to drama.

Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia are two progressive neurological conditions that can affect memory, thinking, behavior, and a person’s ability to perform everyday activities.

According to the National Institute on Aging (NIA), both conditions can cause dementia, a term used to describe a decline in cognitive abilities severe enough to interfere with daily life.

Alzheimer’s disease is the most common cause of dementia. The condition is associated with abnormal buildups of proteins called amyloid and tau in the brain, which disrupt communication between nerve cells and contribute to their damage.

Industry observers note that the NIA states that memory problems are often among the earliest symptoms of Alzheimer’s. As the disease progresses, people may experience increasing difficulty with language, reasoning, decision making, and recognizing familiar people.

Lewy body dementia, meanwhile, is associated with abnormal deposits of a protein called alpha-synuclein in the brain. These deposits, known as Lewy bodies, affect brain chemicals involved in thinking, movement, mood, and sleep, according to the NIA.

People with Lewy body dementia may experience changes in attention and alertness, visual hallucinations, muscle stiffness, difficulty walking, and sleep disturbances.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, the two conditions may co-occur, and their overlapping symptoms may make diagnosis more challenging.

Currently, neither condition has a cure, but treatments are available to help manage symptoms. Certain medications can also slow cognitive decline in some people with early Alzheimer’s disease.

Tesla Cybercab has crashed 8 times, and the data shows a speed problem
